extracted.intended_audience: researchers conducting and reporting in vivo (animal) experiments; authors preparing preclinical manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for transparent reporting of the design, conduct, analysis, and exclusions in preclinical in vivo experiments to improve reproducibility and assess internal validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting exclusions, losses, and outlier handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit description of whether researchers were blinded to the group allocations when data or animals were excluded. Explicitly state where built-in models in statistics packages have been used to remove outliers (e.g. GraphPad Prism’s outlier test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All animals and data used in the experiment should be accounted for. Report losses and exclusions (e.g. illness, mortality, biologically implausible values) and the reason for them so readers can interpret the analysis and replicate methods. State whether exclusions were made blinded to group allocation. If statistical/software outlier-removal routines were used, name them and state where they were applied. Examples in the guidance show descriptions of animals removed for illness, failure to meet inclusion criteria, or procedural errors, and specify the outlier test and cut-off (e.g. Cook’s D > 0.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact sample sizes (n) for each analysis (3c)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each analysis, report the exact value of n in each experimental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the exact number of experimental units analysed in each group (the n number) unambiguously. Account for all animals and data used. Give absolute numbers (e.g. 10/20 rather than 50%). For longitudinal measurements, explicitly report which animals were measured at which time points. Reporting losses/exclusions helps readers assess design, replicate methods, and track discrepancies between planned and analysed sample sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation — state use and method (4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether randomisation was used to allocate experimental units to control and treatment groups. If done, provide the method used to generate the randomisation sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the type of randomisation used (simple, stratified, randomised complete blocks, etc.), the method used to generate the sequence (e.g. computer-generated algorithm, online random number generator, RAND() in spreadsheets), and what was randomised (treatment to experimental unit, order of treatment, etc.). If randomisation was not used, state this explicitly and explain group formation. Explain allocation concealment as part of allocation procedures. Note that simple randomisation can lead to imbalance in small samples; consider matched pairs, blocking, or minimisation to balance important variables. Provide examples and references. If blocking factors are used for randomisation, they should also be included in the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation strategy to minimise confounders (4b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strategy used to minimise potential confounders such as the order of treatments and measurements, or animal/cage location. If confounders were not controlled, state this explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify likely nuisance variables (time/day, litter/cage/tank, investigator/surgeon, equipment, baseline measurements, animal characteristics, location on rack). Report actions taken to manage them: standardising procedures, randomising sampling or measurement order, blocking, or counterbalancing (e.g. cage/tank position). If constraints prevent randomisation, state how these variables were handled in the analysis. Provide practical examples (randomising test time, blocking by body weight, randomising cage selection) to illustrate acceptable strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe who was aware of the group allocation at the different stages of the experiment (during the allocation, the conduct of the experiment, the outcome assessment, and the data analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether blinding/allocation concealment was used at each stage (allocation, conduct, outcome assessment, data analysis) and what specific treatment/condition investigators were blinded to or aware of. Explain steps taken to enable blinding (e.g. separate personnel for allocation, coded syringes, third-party analysis). If blinding was not possible for some stages, give reasons (e.g. overt phenotype, welfare/safety constraints) and describe mitigations (automated measurement, third-party analysis, coding data prior to analysis). Emphasise that blinding reduces bias, especially for subjective outcome assessments, and that analysts should be blinded to specific treatments (group labels can be coded) so semi‑subjective decisions (transformations, handling missing data/outliers) are not biased. If no blinding was used, explicitly state this and justify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define all outcome measures (6a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcome measures assessed (e.g. cell death, molecular markers, or behavioural changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe what was measured and how (operationalise measures where ambiguity exists — e.g. activity as time moving vs distance travelled). State how outcome measures relate to study objectives. Measures should be collected in an unbiased manner where possible (e.g. blinded assessment). Failure to disclose all measured outcomes introduces outcome reporting bias; be comprehensive and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome for hypothesis-testing studies (6b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For hypothesis-testing studies, specify the primary outcome measure, i.e. the outcome measure that was used to determine the sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the single primary outcome (the one used for the sample size calculation) and state whether it was defined prior to data collection. If multiple outcomes are assessed in exploratory studies, a single primary outcome is not required but should be declared if the study purports to test a hypothesis. Registering a protocol in advance is recommended to prevent selective outcome reporting and primary outcome switching. If no primary outcome was pre-specified, explicitly state this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — details and software (7a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of the statistical methods used for each analysis, including software used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide statistical methods a priori and report them. Include the analytical approach for each outcome, specific tests and models used, handling of missing data, data transformations, criteria for treating outliers, inclusion of blocking factors or covariates, measures of central tendency and dispersion reported, assumption checks, and the software (and preferably version) used to perform analyses. Where appropriate, explain implications for analysis (e.g. include blocking factors used in randomisation in the model).
